rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty and measure how the critical pairs respond to slope. The initial run has substantial resolution margin and all compounds elute well before the gradient ends.

Keep the faster gradient and raise temperature to test whether selectivity can separate the compressed central cluster. Higher temperature should also shorten the last peak's retention, preserving the low time penalty.

Test just below 60 C to reopen the new close pair while retaining much of the improved separation in the central cluster. This gradient already keeps the time penalty at zero, so temperature-driven selectivity is the priority.

Lowering temperature should reopen the pair that became critical at 55–60 C, while a steeper gradient may counteract compression of the other central pair. Test this combination to balance both separations while maintaining zero time penalty.

Explore the low-temperature selectivity regime at the established fast gradient. Cooling may separate the central pair on the opposite side of its elution-order crossover while retaining adequate separation elsewhere.

Slightly flatten the gradient at the best temperature to improve the current limiting pair. Comparing directly with injection 4 will show whether the neighboring central pair remains separated as slope decreases.

Injection 7 has reached the maximum possible CRF and remains the benchmark. Test a slightly higher starting organic fraction to seek another maximum-score method with more separation margin around the narrowly resolved central pair.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness to improve the limiting separation from injection 8 while preserving its modest gain for the other central pair. The final organic fraction remains comfortably above the observed elution window; injection 7 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Test the intermediate slope between injections 8 and 9 to seek maximum CRF with a shorter run than injection 9. Interpolation suggests the limiting pair may remain just above R = 1.5 while the other central pair retains adequate separation.

Test a narrower, shifted gradient window to seek a larger minimum-resolution margin while retaining maximum CRF. Relative to injection 9, the higher starting organic fraction may improve the central pair, while the shallower slope should help preserve separation of the competing close pair.

Trim the unused high-organic portion of injection 7 while preserving its starting composition, temperature, and gradient slope exactly. All peaks should elute before the new gradient endpoint, so this method should retain the maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Test a slope between injections 9 and 10 to balance their two limiting separations, targeting both above R = 1.5. This should shorten retention slightly relative to injection 9 while preserving maximum CRF; the endpoint remains above the last peak's estimated elution composition.

With maximum CRF already secured, test whether a shallower gradient at 60 C can resolve its previously coeluting pair while preserving the stronger separation elsewhere. This probes an alternative temperature regime for a maximum-score method with greater resolution margin.

Test a faster, higher-starting-organic method at 60 C to separate the limiting pair on the opposite side of its selectivity crossover. Maximum CRF is already secured; this explores whether comparable separation is possible with substantially shorter retention.

Return to the successful 55 C regime and slightly flatten injection 11's gradient to improve its limiting pair while retaining the other pair's resolution margin. This tests another potential maximum-score method near the zero-time-penalty boundary.

Reduce the slope slightly from injection 16 to bring its limiting pair above R = 1.5 while preserving the other central pair's margin. The last peak is estimated to elute near 9 minutes, potentially retaining zero time penalty and matching the maximum CRF.

Refine around injection 7 with a slightly shallower gradient to improve the R = 1.59 pair while checking that the R = 1.52 pair remains adequately separated. Retention should remain within the zero-time-penalty window, targeting another maximum-score method.

Slightly flatten injection 9's gradient to test the slower edge of its maximum-score region. Its limiting pair has more margin than injection 18's, and the last peak should still elute within the zero-time-penalty window.

Test an intermediate slope between maximum-score injections 9 and 19, where both critical pairs should remain above R = 1.5 and the time penalty should remain zero. Injection 7 remains the established global-maximum benchmark.

Trim injection 9's gradient while preserving its slope, starting composition, and temperature. Its last peak should still elute before the gradient ends at the outlet, retaining maximum CRF with a lower final organic fraction and shorter programmed gradient.

Preserve injection 7's successful slope, starting composition, and temperature while trimming the endpoint to just above the last peak's estimated elution composition. This should match the maximum CRF with all ten peaks still eluting during the gradient.

Slightly flatten injection 20's gradient to test another nearby maximum-score method. The observed slope trends predict adequate separation of both critical pairs and last-peak retention below the approximately 9-minute zero-penalty boundary.

Test a lower endpoint with a slope just shallower than injection 23, targeting retention below 9 minutes and both critical resolutions above 1.5. The final peak may enter the hold briefly, but the nearby successful runs suggest little risk of truncation.

Finish with a slope between maximum-score injections 19 and 20, using an endpoint comfortably above the last peak's elution composition. Both critical pairs should remain above R = 1.5 with zero time penalty; injection 7 already secures the maximum possible CRF.
